name: The Creature from the Black Lagoon
description: An amphibious humanoid from the Amazon
origin: Hollywood original, inspired by an Amazonian tale

film.title: Creature from the Black Lagoon
film.note: Shot in 3D. The underwater scenes were filmed at Wakulla Springs, Florida.

legend: According to producer William Alland, the idea began at a dinner party where the cinematographer Gabriel Figueroa told a legend about a half-man, half-fish creature living in the Amazon. The finished film sends scientists upriver after a fossilised webbed hand from the Devonian period, when life first crawled onto land. It was the last of the great Universal monsters, arriving just as the 1950s 3D craze peaked.

myths.claim: Makeup chief Bud Westmore designed the Creature.
myths.explanation: Artist Milicent Patrick designed it. Westmore took the credit and her role was downplayed for decades.
It was shot with a dual-camera 3D rig, though many cinemas also showed it flat.
Ben Chapman wore the suit on land, while champion swimmer Ricou Browning performed the underwater scenes.

myths.claim: The lagoon scenes were filmed in the Amazon.
myths.explanation: The crew never went to South America. Underwater footage came from Wakulla Springs in Florida and the rest from the Universal lot.

powers: Survives wounds that would kill a man
legacy: Revenge of the Creature (1955), featuring an early screen role for Clint Eastwood
The Shape of Water (2017), Guillermo del Toro's love letter to the Gill-man
facts: The Creature is also known as the Gill-man
Milicent Patrick designed the Creature, but her credit was denied for decades
Two performers shared the role: Ben Chapman on land and Ricou Browning underwater
The underwater scenes were filmed at Wakulla Springs in Florida
The film was released in 3D at the height of the 1950s 3D craze
The expedition begins with a fossilised hand from the Devonian period
hostIntro: Fancy a swim? Tonight we paddle up the Amazon to meet a gentleman with gills, scales and absolutely no respect for personal space.
